section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Cutting Plane
section_1.content: Define a double cone and a cutting plane. Introduce the 'Conic Sections' (ellipse, parabola, hyperbola) based on the angle of intersection between the plane and the cone's axis.
section_1.example: Use a flashlight beam against a wall: tilting the flashlight changes the shape of the light spot from a circle to an ellipse, then a parabola.

section_2.title: Introducing the Dandelin Spheres
section_2.content: Introduce the 'Dandelin Sphere'—a sphere placed inside the cone such that it is tangent to both the cone and the cutting plane. Explain the point of tangency.
section_2.example: Imagine a bouncy ball trapped inside an ice cream cone, touching both the cone's inner walls and the glass lid placed at an angle.

section_3.title: The Mathematical Magic: Proving the Ellipse
section_3.content: Explain the key proof: The distance from any point on the intersection curve to the two tangency points (the foci) is constant. Use animation to show the equal tangent segments from a point to a sphere.
section_3.example: Visualizing a string stretched between two pins (the foci) creating an ellipse, matching the distances to the Dandelin spheres.

section_4.title: Connecting Shapes to Spheres
section_4.content: Briefly describe how adding a second sphere allows us to generalize the proof for parabolas (one sphere) and hyperbolas (spheres in different nappes of the cone).
section_4.example: A satellite dish (parabola) uses one sphere principle; a hourglass-shaped nuclear cooling tower (hyperboloid) uses two spheres.

section_5.title: Summary and Real-world Synthesis
section_5.content: Conclude by linking the abstract geometry of the spheres back to the physical properties of conic sections: focus, directrix, and eccentricity.
section_5.example: Planetary orbits: Planets move in ellipses where the sun sits at one of the focal points defined by the Dandelin logic.

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Adjusted grid to be on the right side
                x = 2.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
